facts.claim: The IEA estimates global data centre electricity consumption at approximately 415 TWh in 2024, around 1.5% of global electricity consumption.
facts.quote: Global electricity consumption by data centres is projected to reach around 945 TWh by 2030 in the Base Case, representing just under 3% of total global electricity consumption in 2030. This is more than double the estimated approximately 415 TWh for 2024 (Figure 2.10), which accounted for around 1.5% of today’s global electricity demand.

sources.title: Energy and AI (World Energy Outlook Special Report)

facts.notes: Same 2024 baseline repeated in the IEA April 2026 update ("from around 415 TWh in 2024"). Covers all data-centre workloads, of which AI is a subset.

facts.claim: The latest IEA update puts data centre electricity consumption at 485 TWh in 2025 and projects roughly 950 TWh in 2030, around 3% of global electricity demand.
facts.quote: Our updated projections see electricity consumption from data centres roughly doubling from 485 TWh in 2025 to 950 TWh in 2030, accounting for around 3% of global electricity demand by that date.

sources.title: Key Questions on Energy and AI (World Energy Outlook Special Report)

facts.notes: Elsewhere the same document says consumption grew "by more than 15% between 2024 and 2025, adding around 70 TWh" to "almost 500 TWh". The April 2025 edition gave ~945 TWh for 2030 in the Base Case; the 2026 update says ~950 TWh.

facts.claim: Data centre electricity consumption grew by more than 15% between 2024 and 2025, adding around 70 TWh; the combined consumption of four major hyperscalers grew 20% in 2024 to 110 TWh.

The combined electricity consumption of four major hyperscalers grew by 20% in 2024, the most recent full year for which data are available, reaching 110 TWh.

sources.title: Key Questions on Energy and AI (World Energy Outlook Special Report)

facts.claim: In the IEA Lift-Off Case data centre electricity consumption reaches over 1 260 TWh by 2030; in the High Efficiency Case around 800 TWh and in the Headwinds Case around 670 TWh.

facts.notes: Central estimate 2.26e-4 deaths/t; range spans zero at the low end. The paper states the reciprocal directly: adding 4,434 metric tons in 2020 causes one excess death in expectation 2020-2100. Temperature-related mortality only. Conversion: deaths = Mt x 226 (e.g. 15.6 Mt private aviation in one year -> ~3,500 expected excess deaths 2020-2100; derived, applies a 2020 marginal value to later emissions).
